text: Match night and my fries took 75 minutes, then arrived cold enough to count as salad. Never ordering during a game again.
cheese toast taste mein sahi tha par aate aate thanda ho gaya. rider ne bola match ki wajah se cafe pe bheed thi.
Cold brew is the safest delivery bet on this menu. Chilled, sealed, chocolatey as promised even mid-match.
Ordered one thing, received something else entirely at 9 pm on a festival night. Not amused.
Paneer tikka sandwich still warm, the foil wrap holding its heat. Delivery did right by me on a busy night.
Rider waited half an hour at the cafe and messaged me twice. The cold brew itself was fine - the delay was not.
Avocado toast reached me in 40 minutes on a match night and was still fresh. A rare win for delivery.
Ordered a strawberry shake, got a rose milk instead, warm-ish and leaking through the lid.
Croissant arrived cool but uncrushed - the paper sleeve saved it. I would reorder on a quieter night.
Waffle in a vented box, berries separate, maple on the side. Whoever designed the packing gets it.
The app said 35 minutes; my order took 85 and arrived stone cold. Cricket evenings break this kitchen.
Cinnamon roll arrived still soft with the extra icing I had asked for. A mid-match delivery that landed.
Waffle arrived limp and cold, the syrup long soaked in. Twenty more overs and I would have forgotten it.
Cheesecake in a chilled sleeve, not a smudge on the glaze. Festival-night delivery done properly.
Hot chocolate arrived genuinely hot - the insulated sleeve worked. A small miracle on a festival night.
Bag arrived sideways: the drink had pooled at the bottom and soaked everything else. Straight into the bin.
Rose latte arrived a little late but still fragrant and neatly sealed. Festival surge forgiven.
Matcha whisked to order and still warm at my door on festival night. Consistency you can taste.
Festival-eve team order of 14: three cappuccinos missing and the muffins squashed under the coffee carrier.
Twenty croissants for a festival morning meeting - boxed in fours, all accounted for, minimal crumbs.
Bulk order for 15 in Diwali week: six items wrong or missing, 90 minutes total. Breakfast became lunch.
11 ka order meeting se pehle pahunch gaya, par aadhe lids dheeli the aur do cup leak ho gaye.
Sixteen muffins for the office party - every one boxed, none squashed, one wrong flavour in the lot.
All 12 paneer tikka sandwiches arrived labelled and upright even on festival night. The packaging held.
Office order during the match: half the items missing, bags unlabelled, everyone ate someone else's dinner.
das sandwich festival working lunch ke liye - 70 min late hue, par sab sahi tha. order pehle karna chahiye.
Nine cappuccinos in one carrier, lids taped, names marked - all nine correct on festival eve.
Twelve drinks on festival eve, ready the minute I reached. Names written on every cup. Organised.
Picked up the office order myself to skip the surge - two wrong drinks in a bag of eight and no apology.
office ke liye 9 latte liye match ke din. do cappuccino ban gaye the aur counter pe 20 min lag gaye.
Festival crowd meant 12 minutes for an espresso. The shot itself was fine; the queue was not.
Counter was drowning in delivery tickets. My drink took forever while riders hovered. Skip match days.
Espresso out in three minutes flat before the match rush built. This is the brew I count on.
Cappuccino sealed under a lid that actually holds, croissant in its own sleeve. Survived the commute.
120 rupees and still a quarter-hour wait in the evening rush. Delivery bags won again.
Pre-match queue was long but it moved; latte in hand in eight minutes. Acceptable for the rush.
Eighteen minutes for a single drink on a weekday. Delivery tickets got priority over humans at the counter.
Pre-match takeaway: my order was ready before my turn at the counter even ended. Blink and done.
Braced for a long match-eve queue but my cappuccino was out in five minutes. Credit to the bar.
Match crowd at the counter, one person billing, my drink took 15 minutes and nobody apologised.
match se pehle ki bheed, 10 min ka wait, par 230 ka latte worth tha. crowd ke hisaab se fast the.
Counter handed my drink to a rider's order by mistake, then remade it. Twenty minutes gone.
Filter coffee to the office during the match - arrived lukewarm after an hour. Won't repeat that.
Desk delivery on match night: cappuccino lukewarm by arrival but the heart pour survived the trip.
ek chai kulhad mein, match screen pe, aur pura cafe ek saath cheer kar raha tha. vibe hi alag thi.
match ke din fries 160 mein portion chhota laga, par taste theek tha. bheed zyada thi bas.
no seat, standing room only, sab match dekh rahe the. hum order bhi nahi kar paye, nikal gaye.
cheese toast sahi tha par match ke time bheed bahut. 20 min table ke liye wait karna pada.
140 ki chai, free match screening, pura crowd saath chillata hua. best evening this month.
Full house for the final over and nobody asked us to leave. Cheap ticket, priceless evening.
four of us, do cheese toast split, match on, bill under 700. seats cramped par paisa vasool.
toast 8 min mein ready tha par bhai 260 for a cheese toast? student budget pe heavy pada.
order 55 min late, toast thanda aur soggy. match exciting tha, food bilkul nahi.
last over khatam, fries abhi tak nahi aaye. aaye toh thande the. worst timing ever.
fries ghar tak crisp pahunche, match ke liye perfect. peri-peri dust on point, full paisa vasool.
Fries were salted right but took an hour on match night. The peri-peri dust deserved better timing.
order split with roommates: fries, do chai, sab garam aaya. match night sorted under 450 total.
Cheese toast arrived cold, the bread gone soft in its own steam. The match was better than dinner.
Fries still had a crunch on arrival which surprised me for match night. Salt level spot on.
muffin thoda thanda aaya aur 160 mein size bhi chhota. match mein busy the toh adjust kar liya.
Fairy lights for festival week, a rose latte and that basque cheesecake. Indiranagar at its prettiest.
Waffle came out crisp despite the match-day rush; only gripe is we were squeezed by the door.
They let us linger through the last over before serving dessert. Cheesecake after a chase is elite.
Flat white silky as always; we just had to shout over the match commentary.
Festival week means extra lights, sweet things, and staff who still find you a seat. Lovely.
rose latte badhiya thi aur festival crowd ke baawajood do seat mil gayi. lucky evening.
Cheesecake flawless; sharing a pushed-together table with strangers shouting at a screen, less so.
They dimmed the lights for the festival evening and our waffle arrived like a small celebration.
Split-flap board flipping, the crowd murmuring at the score, warm light. Didn't even order much.
Waffle a touch soft after the ride but the flavour held up; maple packed separately. Would repeat.
Rose latte delivered during the festival fireworks, still fragrant. Slight spill in the lid - minor.
Dessert reached chilled and unsquashed on the loudest cricket night of the season. Impressed.
croissant flat ho ke aaya aur thanda tha. itni khoobsurat layering, bag ne sab maar diya.
Tried to work through a T20 evening - cheering every over. Left with my drink half finished.
Thought I would work the evening; the match crowd turned the cafe into a stadium. The coffee was decent, at least.
Claimed the corner before the match crowd. Two hours of quiet work and a perfect iced latte.
Found a plug, the cold brew stayed cold, and match commentary stayed a soft hum. Deep work achieved.
Couldn't hear my own call over the cheering. Both plug points taken, both screens blaring. Left early.
Nursed a pricey drink for two hours before the match crowd took over. Fine if you leave by six.
Laptop out, then the projector went up for the match. Work abandoned, evening spent standing.
Early-evening slot before the match crowd: quiet corner, fast wifi, filter coffee done right.
Zoya kept the corner free till I arrived, even with the match rush building. Cold brew as usual.
Match nights are not work nights - learnt that again. Decent drink, unbearable noise.
match se pehle do ghante kaam ho gaya, cappuccino ke saath. baad mein bheed ne sab kharab kar diya.
250 for a drink I barely enjoyed once the match crowd arrived. This cafe is better before six.
Match on the wall screen, kids happy with their shakes and fries, but we waited 25 minutes beside a loud table.
festival dinner: khana aadha ghanta laga aur delivery bags ke liye baar baar hatna pada. bachche patient rahe, main nahi.
Dev sent a milder arrabbiata for my daughter without being asked. Festival rush, still that attentive.
Festival-eve dinner with kids: happy chaos, and staff who actually smiled at the noise.
festival evening, do bhookhe bachche, khana 40 min late. do baar poocha, koi seedha jawab nahi. bahut kharab.
Kids watched their first match crowd erupt over a wicket while demolishing a waffle and slurping shakes.
Match-night dinner for the kids: fries crisp, shakes thick, everything tight in the pink-stamped bag.
Pasta arrived cold with the box dented; the kids refused it. Festival-surge excuses only go so far.
Waffle boxes taped shut so nothing slid; shakes thick on arrival. Kids' festival dinner, sorted.
Kids' shakes and muffins arrived without spills during the festival rush. Happy children.
Cheese toast and fries a touch cold but edible. Festival surge, I get it - still paying full price.
Kids' fries and hot chocolate both arrived cold after the longest festival-night wait. Bedtime won instead.
Two hot chocolates arrived actually hot on festival night, lids taped. Kids asleep happy.
Walked in during a cricket evening, got a dabarah filter coffee, and the whole room groaned at a wicket. Loved it.
Rose milk while strangers argued about the bowling around us. Not quiet - a very Bengaluru evening.
Matcha during a cricket evening in a pink cafe - oddly perfect. The room felt like one big adda.
Matcha at 290 is steep for a visitor, but watching a cricket crowd in a pink cafe? You pay for the scene.
Server explained the kulhad chai unprompted and the cardamom hit properly. Match chaos, still warm service.
Warned that the cafe gets loud during matches - they undersold it. Couldn't hear each other, left early.
Locals taught us when to cheer; the dabarah filter coffee was a bonus. Fun chaos.
Filter coffee and masala chai, one of each, both excellent. The match crowd made it a memory.
Rose milk with sabja seeds while the room held its breath through the last over. Unforgettable first visit.
Queued behind a wall of delivery riders for ten minutes, but the kulhad chai travelled well. Worth it.
Same filter coffee, same dabarah froth, even with half the city ordering during the match. Consistent.
In and out in seven minutes with a croissant even as festival deliveries piled up. They know their regulars.
Festival rush and still: my usual sleeved, bag folded, out in four minutes. Machine of a counter.
queue delivery pickups ke peeche dheere chali aur mera usual phir mehenga ho gaya. abhi bhi loyal hoon.
Loyalty has limits when your ticket is lost between delivery orders twice in one month.
Kabir saved us the corner table before the match started. Kulhad chai and a win - perfect evening.
Meera remembered I take the flat white extra hot. Years in, they still get it right.
mera usual pichle mahine se mehenga ho gaya hai. taste abhi bhi sahi, par price dheere chadhti ja rahi.
match night yahan ek ritual hai. Dev ne kitchen se wave kiya, mera usual bina bole aa gaya.
Still the best two minutes of my morning. Prices crept up over the year, but fairly.
Even with the match crowd my cappuccino had the heart pour. They have figured the rush out.
Usually flawless, but tonight my order vanished between delivery tickets. One bad evening won't end me.
